# Paid Live Mission 5 — Julius context integrity.
#
# THE DELIVERABLES. Real Sunday Relay files, sliced byte-identical, so the diff
# this mission produces applies straight back to the repository. Unlike Mission
# 4 this is not one file: the integrity layer is worthless unless the compiler
# that every worker packet goes through actually calls it, and unless the
# snapshot that records that packet carries what it decided.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-context-integrity.ts
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-runtime.ts
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-context-snapshot.ts

# WHAT IT REASONS ABOUT. Project Brain v2's trust vocabulary — the standings,
# the provenances, the evidence refs and the claim shape. Mission 4 implemented
# this module's BODIES; this mission consumes its TYPES and its semantics, which
# is what "the trust core participates in context construction" has to mean. The
# integrity layer must not call the functions here: it reads standing off claims
# it is handed, so it works whether or not Mission 4's candidate has landed.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-memory-trust.ts

# IMPORT-CHAIN CLOSURE. `julius-runtime` imports `effectivelyAcceptedTaskIds`
# from here as a VALUE, so this loads at runtime. A slice whose import chain
# stops halfway is a sandbox that works until it doesn't.
#
# AND IT DID. `julius-repair-lineage` later grew a value import of
# `julius-segment-lineage`, and this list did not follow it: provisioning this
# mission and running its own declared test command died on
# ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before a single assertion ran. Nothing caught it, because
# no test provisioned a real mission slice and resolved its imports. One does
# now — `scripts/julius-mission-slice.test.ts`, "every slice mission's import
# chain is closed" — so the next file to grow an import fails `npm test` here
# instead of a paid run there.
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-repair-lineage.ts
src/relay/mission/julius/julius-segment-lineage.ts
